page.layout: One printed page. Running head at the top, with the page number beside it. One column of running text, with a Greek and Latin marginal note at the left, level with the lines "&adiunctorum loci" and "enim tum beneficium". The catchword "&c" stands at the right below the last line.

main_text.l: ne iudicamus: quia honestum: quia lau-
dabile: quia cum virtute coniunctum: &
ad eandem merita atq; beneficia accepta
traducenda sunt omnia: vt illa quoq;
ornari solent, quæ nobis vel summè ne-
cessaria: vel commoda plurima maximá-
que adferunt: vel iucunditatem atque vo-
luptatem aliquam pariunt: aut prædican-
tur ab iis, in quos collata: quæ ad effectus
referuntur. Amplificantia etiam hîc adhi-
benda, quæ comparatorum potissimùm,
& adiunctorū loci suppeditant. Magnum
enim tum beneficium videtur, cùm com-
paratur cum aliis: aut ostéditur: amicum,
vel primum, vel solum, vel inter non pau-
cos præcipuum extitisse, qui beneficium
contulerit. Circumstantiæ itidem rei, per-
sonæ, modi, temporis, loci, sua natura exig-
ua beneficia commendant, augent, am-
plificát: atq; efficiunt, vt grata sint ea: quæ
data vltrò, non precibus atq; intercessio-
ne impetrata: quæ data non temerè, sed
consilio certo: quæ data cum aliquo peri-
culo, aut offensione aliorum: quæ data à
viro magno, summaque authoritate præ-
dito: quæ data indignis, neq; eiuscemodi
aliqua promeritis: quæ data citò, tempe-
stiuè, sæpe: quæ deniq; diuturna, stabilia, &c

page.notes: The Greek marginal word is hard to read at this scan size; it is taken as ἀὐξητικὰ (augmentative) and marked as doubtful. The reading "potissimùm" is taken from the printed form "potifsimùm". The final "&c" is treated as a catchword, since it stands alone below the last line at the right.
